chemistry, and materials science. Your task is to act as a "Novelty Evaluator":
objectively judge whether a newly generated mathematical equation is

- NOT NOVEL: the equation is a well-known classical formula that already exists
  in textbooks, on the internet, or in the open scientific literature — i.e. a

Problem description: A sample of unstable nuclei is prepared and left to decay without replenishment. The number of surviving parent nuclei is monitored over time. [VARIABLES & PARAMETERS]:
- Target variable: dN_dt (Rate of change of the number of surviving parent nuclei)
- Input features: t (time)
- Dynamic states: N (Number of surviving parent nuclei); D (Number of delayed daughter/neutron-precursor nuclei that can regenerate parents via capture); Phi (Neutron flux field driving capture-induced regeneration)
- Parameters: lambda_decay (Decay constant (transition probability per unit time)); beta_stim (Dimensionless enhancement fraction of the decay rate at low population); N_ref (Reference population scale below which self-absorption shielding is lost); gamma_2body (Rate coefficient for density-dependent two-body loss); N_sat (Saturation population above which two-body loss becomes proportional to N); sigma_capture (Rate coefficient for capture-induced regeneration of parents from the daughter pool); kappa_prod (Production rate of daughter precursors per two-body loss event); eta_absorb (Loss rate of daughters via capture back onto parents); mu_leak (Intrinsic escape/decay rate of the daughter precursor pool); alpha_flux (Sensitivity of capture regeneration to the neutron flux field); phi_source (Intrinsic neutron flux source term from two-body loss events); chi_burn (Flux depletion coefficient from absorption on parents/daughters); tau_flux (Intrinsic relaxation/leakage rate of the neutron flux field); rho_ind (Maximum flux-induced parent regeneration rate coefficient at high flux saturation); Phi_thr (Threshold neutron flux above which induced regeneration turns on)

[CANDIDATE EQUATION]:
dN_dt = -lambda_decay * N * (1 + beta_stim * exp(-N / N_ref)) - gamma_2body * N**2 / (N + N_sat) + sigma_capture * D * N * (1 + alpha_flux * Phi) + rho_ind * Phi**2 * N / (Phi**2 + Phi_thr**2)

    },

      "initial_condition": 0.0,
      "description": "Number of delayed daughter/precursor nuclei produced by two-body loss that can regenerate parents"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "Phi",
      "rhs": "phi_source * gamma_2body * N**2 / (N + N_sat) - chi_burn * Phi * N - tau_flux * Phi",
      "initial_condition": 0.0,
      "description": "Neutron flux field sourced by two-body loss events, burned by absorption on nuclei and lost by leakage"
    }
  ]
}
(Note: this equation comes from an equation-evolution pipeline; assume it is
